questions.question: A model team changes its tokenizer and re-runs a filter threshold before training. What should be versioned with the resulting dataset manifest?
options: Only the final row count
The source references, transformation code, configuration, and quality report
Only the model checkpoint
The test accuracy from the previous run
questions.explanation: A reproducible dataset release records both its input sources and the transformations that produced the retained examples.

questions.question: Why might a small reference corpus receive more training weight than a much larger web crawl?
options: It guarantees the model is factually correct
It lets the team avoid recording provenance
It can supply task-relevant, higher-signal coverage that the crawl lacks
It removes the need for validation data
questions.explanation: Mixture weights express the desired learning signal, not a source's raw token count. Smaller sources may fill an important capability gap.

questions.question: A customer appears in both a training row and a test row with different transactions. What split rule best protects the evaluation?
options: Randomly split individual rows again
Keep all records for the customer in one partition
Copy the customer into validation as well
Remove every other transaction
questions.explanation: Grouping by the entity that carries repeated information prevents the model from learning a customer's history and appearing to generalize on that same customer.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes validation data from final test data?
options: Validation trains the model while test data has no labels
Both may guide hyperparameter choices as long as their sizes differ
Validation guides development choices; final test data remains independent of those choices
Final test data should be sampled from training after every experiment
questions.explanation: Using final-test results to select models or settings makes the reported test result optimistic. Validation exists to support development without consuming the final estimate.

questions.question: What does near-duplicate detection add beyond exact file hashing?
options: It catches paraphrases, template variants, and close copies that byte hashes miss
It proves every example has a valid license
It creates labels for unlabeled examples
It ensures every class has the same number of rows
questions.explanation: Exact hashes catch identical bytes. Similarity methods help find records that carry substantially the same content despite small edits or formatting changes.

questions.question: A forecasting dataset includes articles published after the prediction cutoff. What failure has occurred?
options: Class imbalance
Temporal leakage
Underfitting
Tokenization drift
questions.explanation: Future information would not have been available at prediction time, so it inflates offline performance and invalidates the evaluation.
